items.title: Lakers biggest test is coming, but it’s not Spurs, per JJ Redick
items.summary: The Lakers’ biggest test of the season is coming up. It’s not Friday, when they’ll face Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs. It’s Saturday, when the world will be reacting to whatever transpired. “Whether we lose the game, whether we win the game, we’re either going to be contenders on [ESPN’s] ‘First Take’ or we’re not going to be contenders and we’re fake,” Lakers coach JJ Redick said. “That stuff is just noise.”For the Lakers, their upcoming game against the Spurs is a temperature check. The teams are tied for the best record in the NBA at 15-3. And their stars, Luka Doncic and Victor Wembanyama, are in a two-man race for the MVP Award.In other words, this is prime theater. items.title: Sixers Notes: LeBron, Barlow, Wade, Smith, NBA Cup
items.summary: While LeBron James has posted solid numbers for the Sixers this fall, he has been content to play a secondary role, having entered Wednesday’s game vs. Miami as the team’s fourth-leading scorer. However, he showed last night that he’s still capable of submitting a vintage LeBron performance, as he accumulated 25 points, 12 assists, and 10 rebounds for his first triple-double as a 76er. In a seven-point victory, Philadelphia outscored the Heat by 14 points with James on the floor. “I don’t think my job is to dominate the game every night for this ball club,” James said after the victory, per Kris Rhim of ESPN. “… If they need me to dust off the cape from time to time, I can still accomplish that. But that’s not my job. But if they need it, I can do it at any given moment.” As Rhim details, James took over the game for a stretch during the second quarter, scoring 14 straight points for…

items.title: Northwest Notes: Morant, Holiday, Filipowski, Mitchell
items.summary: After playing in the Trail Blazers’ first four games of the season, point guard Ja Morant has been on the shelf since October 29 due to a left hamstring strain. But Morant, who was ruled out for at least four weeks, may not be sidelined for much longer, writes Joe Freeman of The Oregonian (subscription required). As Freeman details, head coach Micah Nori said on Wednesday that Morant has resumed five-on-five work and has a decent chance to return within the next week or so. “I’ll go out on limb and say we’ll see him on this home stand,” Nori said. “He is getting close.” After beating San Antonio on Wednesday in the first game of a five-game home stand, the Blazers will host the Warriors on Friday, the Pelicans on Sunday, the Timberwolves on Tuesday, and the Jazz next Thursday. items.title: And-Ones: Expansion, Parker, Cook, Anderson
items.summary: The NBA appears to be further along on a Las Vegas expansion team than it is on a new Seattle franchise, but the general consensus among current club owners is that they’d like to see two new teams enter the league in the same season, rather than doing so one at a time, ESPN’s Brian Windhorst and Ramona Shelburne said on the Hoop Collective podcast (YouTube link; hat tip to RealGM). items.title: Timberwolves Notes: McDaniels, Ball, Randle
items.summary: Given that Jaden McDaniels still had three guaranteed years remaining on his current contract entering this season, it came as a bit of a surprise when word broke just ahead of opening night that the Timberwolves had agreed to tack another year onto his deal, signing the forward to a one-year, $40MM extension that will cover the 2029/30 season. But McDaniels is showing with his play so far this season why the Wolves felt compelled to lock him up for as long as possible, as Jon Krawczynski writes for The Athletic (free link). Already one of the NBA’s best perimeter defenders, McDaniels has taken his offensive game to a new level this fall, averaging career highs in points (19.2) and assists (3.8) per game, as well as field goal percentage (56.6%). He’s also making a career-best 1.7 three-pointers per game at a rate of 40.7%. The Timberwolves’ road win in Oklahoma City on Wednesday…

items.title: Details On NBA Cup Prize Money For 2026
items.summary: The group stage of the NBA Cup will wrap up this week, with teams playing their final round robin matchups on Friday. By the time those games are complete, seven clubs will have joined the Mavericks in advancing to the knockout round of the league’s in-season tournament. The prize money for the players whose teams make the NBA Cup quarterfinals has once again increased in the fourth year of the event. According to reports from NBC Sports and The Athletic, the bonuses for 2026 are as follows: Players on the team that wins the NBA Cup: $604,985 apiece Players on the team that loses the NBA Cup final: $241,994 apiece Players on the two teams that lose in the NBA Cup semifinals: $120,997 apiece Players on the four teams that lose in the NBA Cup quarterfinals: $60,499 apiece When the Lakers won the inaugural in-season tournament in 2023, those figures were $500K, $200K, $100K, and $50K,…

Dallas is 3-0 in the group, with wins over Houston, Utah and Denver and a +36 point differential. items.title: Jaylen Brown To Undergo Imaging After Leaving Game With Hamstring Tightness
items.summary: Sixers forward Jaylen Brown was removed from Wednesday’s game against Miami after experiencing tightness in his left hamstring, according to Kris Rhim of ESPN. Coach Nick Nurse said medical imaging will take place, and an update on Brown’s condition will be issued on Thursday (Twitter link). Brown exited late in the second quarter after hitting a step-back jumper, Rhim details. He shook his head and grabbed at the hamstring, then signaled to the bench that he needed to be replaced. He finished with six points, one rebound and one assist in 17 minutes as Philadelphia posted a 111-104 victory in the NBA Cup contest. Rhim notes that Brown’s hamstring issues began in a November 16 game against Brooklyn. He tied a season high with 31 points, but had to leave with a hamstring strain and sat out the next two contests against Orlando and Milwaukee. He returned on Monday with 20 points against…

items.title: Mavericks Notes: Martin, Irving, Risacher, Johnson, Lively
items.summary: Caleb Martin’s first full season with the Mavericks was disappointing, but he has emerged as a valuable three-and-D wing this year, writes Eddie Sefko of NBA.com. After being limited to 58 games last season by back, heel and ankle injuries, along with an extended illness, Martin is back to full health and looks more like the player he was earlier in his career. “He’s just comfortable,” P.J. Washington said. “Last year, he was dealing with injuries. This year, he’s more back to himself, finding a rhythm. We love him being out there doing whatever he wants on the defensive end. Obviously, he’s guarding the best guards every night. We need his energy and he creates a lot of fast breaks.” Martin, who has become the on-court leader of an improved Dallas defense, tied a career high with five steals in Tuesday’s win at Denver. He enjoys disrupting opposing offenses and welcomes the challenge…

items.title: Tyrese Haliburton Nears Return From Hamstring Injury
items.summary: Tyrese Haliburton was a full participant in the Pacers’ practice on Wednesday, but a decision hasn’t been made on when he’ll be ready for game action, writes Tony East of Circle City Spin. The star guard, who hasn’t played since straining his left hamstring in an October 26 game, recently posted on social media that he wants to resume playing by the end of the month. Indiana’s only remaining November games are Friday against Philadelphia and Saturday at Chicago, so it’s not clear if he’ll be able to meet that goal. Haliburton, who also practiced on Tuesday with the G League’s Noblesville Boom, believes the sessions are the final step toward being cleared to play, but added that the Pacers’ medical staff is being cautious. “I think, being completely honest, the organization is doing as best they can protecting me from myself, you know,” he told reporters after today’s practice.…
